ops.text: A stale dev build at ~/.local/bin/cc-notes (v0.47.11-0.20260726095120-0b1d14e2b5e0+dirty, built Jul 26) shadows the correct brew install (/opt/homebrew/bin/cc-notes -> Cellar/0.49.0) on PATH, and it cannot read this repo at all: every read fails with "entity kind mismatch: add_anchor on a task" — the exact poison-pill that v0.49's fold forward-compat change (5733259) fixed. So `cc-notes` from a shell in this repo is broken while `go run ./cmd/cc-notes` works, which reads as "cc-notes is broken" rather than "your PATH has a stale shim". Two things made it costly: the error names an entity-kind bug, not a version problem, so the first instinct is to go looking for corrupt data; and `cc-notes --version` was not the thing anyone thought to check, because brew had already been upgraded. Fix on this machine is `rm ~/.local/bin/cc-notes`. Worth considering whether the version banner should appear in the error for a fold failure that forward-compat already handles in a newer binary — a build that predates the tolerant fold literally cannot read repos a newer one wrote, and that is exactly the case where naming the version pays.
